questions.question: On a chest radiograph, the "Westermark sign" of acute pulmonary embolism represents:
choices: Focal oligemia (decreased vascular markings) distal to an embolus
Dilation of the right main pulmonary artery
questions.detail: Westermark sign is a classic but rare sign of PE reflecting reduced perfusion.

questions.question: A peripheral, wedge-shaped opacity on a chest radiograph in a patient with pleuritic chest pain is known as:
questions.detail: This represents a pulmonary infarct distal to a PE.

questions.question: What is the CT hallmark for the diagnosis of Acute Pulmonary Embolism?
questions.detail: On contrast-enhanced CTPA, the embolus appears as a dark filling defect within the bright contrast-filled artery.

questions.question: Chronic Thromboembolic Pulmonary Hypertension (CTEPH) is characterized on CT by which of the following?
choices: Webbing and eccentric calcified thrombi adherent to the vessel wall
questions.detail: Chronic clots become incorporated into the wall, often forming webs or bands.

questions.question: In the evaluation of pulmonary hypertension on CT, a main pulmonary artery diameter greater than what threshold is considered enlarged?
questions.detail: A main PA diameter ≥29 mm is a highly specific indicator of pulmonary hypertension.

questions.question: Mosaic attenuation on CT can be caused by either small airway disease or vascular disease. How does expiratory CT help differentiate them?
choices: Air trapping from airway disease becomes more apparent on expiration
Vascular disease shows air trapping on expiration
Both show the same pattern on expiration
Expiratory CT is only useful for nodules
questions.detail: In small airway disease, the lucent areas remain lucent (trap air), whereas in purely vascular disease, the lucent areas increase in density normally.

questions.question: Right ventricular (RV) strain from a large PE is suggested on CT by:
choices: An RV to LV diameter ratio > 1.0
questions.detail: RV enlargement (ratio > 1.0) and septal bowing are critical signs of acute RV strain.

questions.question: Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension (PAH) is defined hemodynamically by a mean pulmonary artery pressure (mPAP) greater than:
questions.detail: While some recent guidelines use 20 mmHg, 25 remains the classic boards answer for PAH definition.

questions.question: Which vascular anomaly involves a partial anomalous pulmonary venous return (PAPVR) from the right lung to the IVC?
questions.detail: The "scimitar" is the anomalous vein curving toward the diaphragm.

questions.question: Septal lines (Kerley B lines) appearing in a patient with mitral stenosis but NO acute heart failure represent:
questions.detail: In chronic conditions like mitral stenosis, septal lines can become permanent due to fibrosis.

questions.question: The "Knuckle sign" (or Palla sign) refers to:
choices: An abruptly tapering or "chopped off" pulmonary artery due to a large embolus
questions.detail: This is a radiographic sign of a large central PE.

questions.question: A patient with Hereditary Hemorrhagic Telangiectasia (HHT) is most likely to have which pulmonary vascular finding?
questions.detail: HHT (Osler-Weber-Rendu) is strongly associated with pulmonary AVMs, which can cause paradoxical emboli to the brain.
